# Figures

![**Study overview and analytical workflow for quantifying the relative importance of past human activity and palaeoclimate for pollen assemblage properties (PAPs) at different spatial and temporal scales.** From left to right, the diagram shows the proxy-data sources, the variables derived from them, their inferential roles, the spatial units used for analysis, the two hierarchical variation-partitioning (HVarPart) analyses, and the resulting comparison of predictor importance. The source data comprise the original 1,262-record H1 inventory of fossil pollen sequences, archaeological radiocarbon dates summarised as summed probability densities (SPDs), expert-screened pollen indicators of human-impact events, and four CHELSA-TraCE21k palaeoclimate variables: annual mean temperature, minimum temperature of the coldest month, precipitation of the warmest quarter, and precipitation of the coldest quarter. Pollen data were converted to PAPs, whereas the archaeological and climate records represent human activity and palaeoclimate, respectively. H1 partitions variation in PAPs within pollen records and among records across continental groups and regions defined from present-day Köppen–Geiger classes. H2 first summarises temporal changes in relationships among PAPs using principal component analysis and pairwise Procrustes sum-of-squares distances, then partitions these changes between human and climate predictors using distance-based redundancy analysis. Coverage of the three proxy families is shown in @suppfig-pollen-coverage, @suppfig-human-coverage, and @suppfig-event-coverage; example input records are shown in @suppfig-record-examples.](figures/figure-01-study-overview.png){#fig-study-overview width=100% fig-alt="Workflow linking pollen records, human and climate proxies, PAPs, spatial units, HVarPart analyses, and predictor importance."}

![**Temporal trajectories of six pollen assemblage properties (PAPs) from 8.5 to 2.0 ka BP.** Columns represent the continental groups North America, Central and South America, Europe, Asia, and Oceania; rows represent taxonomic richness ($N_0$), the difference between Shannon- and Simpson-effective diversity ($N_1-N_2$), rate of compositional change, detrended canonical correspondence analysis axis 1 (DCCA axis 1), diversity change-point density, and turnover change-point density. Colours identify regions defined from present-day Köppen–Geiger classes. Coloured lines are posterior mean trajectories from the hierarchical generalised additive models, and shaded ribbons are their 95% credible intervals. Each regional trajectory is an equal-weighted average of record-level posterior predictions evaluated only within the observed temporal coverage of each record, so records with longer sequences or denser sampling do not receive greater weight. Missing portions of trajectories indicate insufficient observed coverage. The DCCA-axis sign is arbitrary, and negative values for centred or transformed properties retain their model-scale interpretation rather than representing negative taxon richness, diversity, or ecological rates. Individual displays for all ten PAPs are provided in @suppfig-pap-n0, @suppfig-pap-n1, @suppfig-pap-n2, @suppfig-pap-n1-minus-n2, @suppfig-pap-n2-n1, @suppfig-pap-n1-n0, @suppfig-pap-roc, @suppfig-pap-dcca, @suppfig-pap-density-diversity, and @suppfig-pap-density-turnover.](figures/figure-02-pap-trajectories.png){#fig-pap-trajectories width=100% fig-alt="Temporal trajectories of six pollen assemblage properties by continental group and region."}

![**Relative importance of past human activity and palaeoclimate for spatial variation in pollen assemblage properties from 8.5 to 2.0 ka BP after controlling for time within pollen records.** Each row represents a continental group: North America, Central and South America, Europe, Asia, and Oceania. Maps on the left show the locations of the `r format(spatial_controlled_n, big.mark = ",")` eligible pollen records, coloured by region; only map areas containing records are displayed. The remaining panels show the zero-truncated human-minus-climate balance, which ranges from -1 (all positive hierarchical contribution allocated to climate) through 0 (equal allocation) to +1 (all allocated to human SPD). The continental-group panel shows the density of record-level balances. Coloured circles show the pooled balance for each region, and the vertical lines show the central 50%, 75%, and 95% ranges of record-level balances within that region; regions without an estimable pooled balance are blank. The thick horizontal line repeated across each row is the pooled continental-group balance. For this display, negative signed hierarchical contributions were set to zero before the remaining human and climate components were recomposed to sum to one. Consequently, a displayed zero is not evidence that a driver had no ecological effect. Signed contributions, including negative components arising from suppressor or commonality structure, are shown in @suppfig-signed-results.](figures/figure-03-h1-spatial-controlled.png){#fig-h1-spatial width=100% fig-alt="Maps, record-level densities, and regional summaries of controlled zero-truncated human-minus-climate HVarPart balance."}

![**Relative importance of past human activity, palaeoclimate, and spatial structure for temporal variation in pollen assemblage properties within 500-year time slices.** Rows represent North America, Central and South America, Europe, Asia, and Oceania; columns are 500-year time slices, with the age gradient running from older (8.5 ka BP; dark blue) to younger (0.5 ka BP; light blue). Within each continental group and time slice, the left bar with a solid outline uses archaeological summed probability density (SPD) as the human predictor and the right bar with a dotted outline uses expert-screened human-impact events. Gold and orange segments show the human contribution estimated from SPD and events, respectively; teal segments show palaeoclimate, and purple segments show spatial structure represented by selected distance-based Moran eigenvector maps (dbMEMs). Each bar is a zero-truncated composition: negative signed hierarchical contributions were set to zero and the remaining human, climate, and spatial components were rescaled to sum to one. The SPD comparison is restricted to 8.5–2.0 ka BP and contains `r temporal_spd_n` estimable continental-group–age combinations; event-based bars extend to 0.5 ka BP where available as a separate exploratory proxy-sensitivity display, outside the primary SPD-based inferential interval. Missing bars represent non-estimable continental-group–age–proxy combinations, not zero influence. Signed contributions are shown in @suppfig-temporal-signed.](figures/figure-04-h1-temporal-controlled.png){#fig-h1-temporal width=87% fig-alt="Paired continental-group temporal bars showing zero-truncated human, climate, and spatial contributions for SPD and event proxies."}
